note.note:
Subjective:
- Chief complaint: “My right ankle has been hurting and swollen for two days.”
- History of presenting complaint: Patient reports rolling her right ankle while stepping off a curb two days ago. Noted immediate pain and swelling, with difficulty bearing weight but able to walk with limp. No numbness, tingling, or discoloration. No open wounds.
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Medications: None reported.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Social history: Lives alone, walks daily for exercise, no tobacco, no alcohol.

Objective:
- Right ankle: Swelling noted laterally. Tenderness on palpation over lateral malleolus. No deformity or open wounds. Bruising present. Range of motion decreased due to pain, unable to fully dorsiflex or plantarflex. Can bear weight with difficulty (limping). No neurovascular deficit; pulses palpable, sensation intact.
- No other injuries noted.
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Investigations: X-ray of right ankle ordered, results pending.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue: Right ankle pain and swelling post-injury
   - Assessment: Suspected right lateral ankle sprain versus fracture.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Lateral ankle sprain (high likelihood; mechanism, swelling, tenderness over lateral malleolus).
     - Ankle fracture (moderate likelihood; inability to fully bear weight, localized bony tenderness).
     - Peroneal tendon injury (possible; mechanism and swelling).
   - Investigations planned: Right ankle X-ray (to rule out fracture).
   - Treatment planned: RICE (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) advised. Ankle brace recommended. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) suggested (dose/route/frequency not documented). Advised avoidance of weight-bearing activities until imaging results.
   - Relevant referrals: None at this stage.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Medication list, allergies, and vitals not documented; consider systems review for indirect injuries. No pain scale documented.
● Internal conflicts: No conflicts between transcript and DDx.
● Transcript quality: Clear, complete; no evident technical issues.
